title: task-query-grammar — case shape (v0.1)
description: Pins the closed task-query grammar (src/notes/taskQuery.ts in the main myne repository; markdown-dialect.md §3.9) — BOTH what it accepts and what it refuses. A parse-only vector set would still pass for a port that accepted one extra clause, so the drop cases are where the closedness claim actually lives: all THREE function-valued forms (naming only the filtering one and silently accepting the others would break the claim), a field name in a value position (the boundary rule — a field name may never appear where a value goes), arithmetic over a field, and out-of-roster words. The 'refuse' cases pin the widen guard: a query whose clauses were ALL dropped must not collapse to matching everything, because a misunderstood query rendering the whole vault looks like a correct enormous result — while a genuinely empty query is legitimately unfiltered. Not an on-disk codec and not cryptographic; deterministic cross-client behaviour. TS-runner category (no Rust generator).

vector_id.description: Stable identifier of the form 'task-query-grammar/v0.1/<slug>'. Immutable once shipped.

case_kind.description: parse: every clause understood (no warnings, not refused). drop: some clauses dropped while the rest still execute. refuse: every clause dropped, so the query refuses rather than widening.

query.description: The query body, exactly as it appears between the fence markers. May be empty — an empty query is legitimately unfiltered, which is the distinction the widen guard rests on.

expected_clause_kinds.description: The clause kinds the parser produced, in source order. The roster is closed: only these eight names may appear.

expected_dropped.description: Clauses the parser could not read. Each names the source text VERBATIM — the widget shows the user what they actually wrote — and a stable machine-readable reason.

text.description: The dropped clause, verbatim (trimmed, case as written).

reason.description: function-valued: one of the three function forms. expression: a shape that reads a field and operates on it. malformed-value: a recognized clause whose value is outside the closed value union — including a bare field name. unrecognized: outside the roster entirely.

expected_refused.description: True only when EVERY clause was dropped and at least one was written. A parser must never let this collapse to 'match everything'.
